clue.text: A dog is put outside in a pram

indicators.note: the dog's name is wrapped around the little word that follows

parts.note: a basset is a short-legged hound
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tucks a dog into a baby carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is put outside' puts BASSET around IN; the 'A' at the start is just an article. A bassinet is a hooded baby carriage or cradle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassinet is a hooded wicker cradle or perambulator, the sort of carriage a baby rides in.

clue.text: Public house?

definitions.meaning: the people watching or listening, as in 'the reading public'
in a theatre the house is the crowd in the seats

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name the spectators: the general following of a performer, and the crowd filling a theatre.

clue.text: Removing a coat — or much more!

definitions.text: Removing a coat — or much more!

parts.words: Removing a coat — or much more!
parts.note: taking off one garment innocently, or a striptease where everything comes off

explanation.definitionFit: Shedding clothing describes both slipping off a jacket and undressing completely.

clue.text: Fixed form of denial

indicators.note: a new form of the word means its letters take another shape

explanation.surface: A kind of denial that is fixed and unshakeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hammered in place with nails is secured, fastened.

clue.text: His victims got it in the neck

definitions.text: His victims got it in the neck

parts.words: His victims got it in the neck
parts.note: the idiom for being punished, read literally: the original Indian cult members strangled their victims

explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from the Indian Thuggee, robbers who strangled travellers; today it means any violent ruffian.

clue.text: His work often figures in art exhibitions

definitions.text: His work often figures in art exhibitions

parts.words: His work often figures in art exhibitions
parts.note: 'figures' looks like a verb meaning appears, but his work is figures: statues

explanation.definitionFit: A carver of statues makes figures that are shown in galleries.

clue.text: Hitch in banknote production

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A snag holds up the printing of banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals a run of letters inside 'banknote'; 'production' completes the picture of a printing works.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a kind of tied loop used by sailors and climbers to fasten a rope.

clue.text: Henry measures the rigging

parts.note: Hal is the familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
yards are units of length

explanation.surface: A man called Henry takes measurements of a ship's ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: Halyards are the ropes for hoisting sails and flags, part of a vessel's tackle.

clue.text: I can head this way for the ranch

indicators.note: the words are to be arranged in a particular way, read as an instruction to rearrange

explanation.surface: A traveller says he will set off in this direction for the ranch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this way' looks like directions, but it tells you to arrange the letters of 'I can head' in a new way.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large estate or ranch in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: River that's Polish — or German

definitions.meaning: a waterway flowing through Poland to the Baltic
the German word meaning 'or'

explanation.definitionFit: The river forms much of the Polish border with Germany, and in German the same word is the conjunction meaning either-or.

clue.text: False registration made by a criminal

definitions.meaning: an unlawful item written into a register or ledger
a burglar breaking into a building

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a fraudulent record in a book, the other a break-in by a burglar.

clue.text: Idle? Definitely not

definitions.meaning: doing no work at all
a colloquial flat refusal

explanation.definitionFit: Literally being inactive, and also an informal phrase of outright refusal.

clue.text: Where to find an angry rice-farmer?

definitions.text: Where to find an angry rice-farmer?

parts.words: Where to find an angry rice-farmer?
parts.note: a paddy is a rice field and also a fit of temper

explanation.definitionFit: A rice-grower works in a flooded field, and a paddy is also a British word for a tantrum.

clue.text: Return to surrender

definitions.meaning: the profit an investment produces
give way, give up

explanation.definitionFit: It means both the income a crop or investment produces and giving way to pressure.

clue.text: Summer, almost fall

definitions.meaning: read as 'one who sums', someone who adds up or totes up figures
stagger, nearly topple over

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who adds up totals tots them, and to stagger unsteadily is to nearly topple.

clue.text: Grasping what is meant by average

definitions.meaning: miserly, tight-fisted
the look-alike run in 'meant' is a coincidence, not a hidden word

explanation.definitionFit: Stingy with money, and the statistical average of a set of numbers.

clue.text: The most important guy on board

definitions.meaning: the chief support, the thing everything depends on
a guy is a rope or wire, and on a sailing ship this one braces the mainmast

explanation.definitionFit: Literally the stay rope supporting a ship's mainmast, and figuratively the chief support of anything.

clue.text: Make a profit and brighten up

definitions.meaning: earn as net gain, as in ... a thousand pounds
as weather does when clouds part

explanation.definitionFit: To net a sum after expenses, and for skies to become bright and cloudless.

clue.text: Lime and cats affected plant

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed or altered, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lime and cats have damaged a plant in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a climbing garden plant with showy flowers.

clue.text: Oxford rowing crew is encored

indicators.note: an encore is a repeat performance, so the word is said twice

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Oxford eight is called back for another race.
explanation.walkthrough: Isis is the Oxford name for the Thames and the name of Oxford's reserve boat in the Boat Race against Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford University reserve boat in the annual Boat Race bears the name of the river through Oxford.

clue.text: Finally need hint perhaps to solve this clue

indicators.note: the letters may perhaps be arranged otherwise, signalling a reshuffle

explanation.surface: A solver admits they may need a hint to crack this clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges NEED HINT; 'to solve this clue' is a playful link.
explanation.definitionFit: At last, after everything, is an adverb meaning eventually or ultimately.

clue.text: Soldier points out other ranks' neglect

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the pieces are put out of order and rearranged

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
N and E are compass points
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, the non-officers

explanation.surface: A soldier complains that the rank and file are being neglected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GI, NE and OR into a new order. Other ranks are soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to disregard it, to pay it no attention.

clue.text: The Spanish, say, take time out to find a deputy

indicators.note: the date lies outside, wrapped around the other pieces

parts.note: a date is a point in time
el is Spanish for 'the'
eg, for example

explanation.surface: Someone takes time off to find a stand-in, perhaps in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' puts DATE around EL and EG; 'take' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegate is a person sent to act or speak for others, a representative.

clue.text: Instruction used in the services?

parts.note: it looks like military training, but in church services a passage from the Bible is read aloud

explanation.definitionFit: A unit of teaching, and also a Bible passage read during church worship.

clue.text: US city casinos possibly accepting foreign currency

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in another piece
the letters might possibly form something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the franc was the money of France

explanation.surface: Gambling dens in an American city may take money from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges CASINOS to SANCISCO, and 'accepting' places FRANC inside it after SAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Californian port on the Golden Gate is a major American city.

clue.text: New line that starts from Victoria

indicators.note: a new arrangement of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A new railway line starts out from Victoria station.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria looks like the London rail terminus, but it is Lake Victoria in Africa, from which the river flows north.
explanation.definitionFit: The White Nile flows out of Lake Victoria in East Africa, its usual source.

clue.text: French river, dear to those living nearby

definitions.meaning: a tributary of the Loire in central France
the French word for dear, as used by people in France

explanation.definitionFit: A tributary of the Loire, and also the French adjective meaning beloved.

clue.text: Aide contrived a plan

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: A notion or scheme for doing something is a thought or plan.

clue.text: A case is essential back in Lincoln

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln's nickname

indicators.note: the word is turned around and read in the opposite direction

parts.note: vital, absolutely necessary

explanation.surface: A legal case is essential to Abraham Lincoln's past as a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns VITAL to LATIV, and 'in' places it inside ABE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin grammar the ablative is a noun case expressing means, place or separation.

clue.text: He goes from one side to the other

definitions.text: He goes from one side to the other

parts.words: He goes from one side to the other
parts.note: not a traveller crossing a road but someone deserting to the opposing camp

explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat deserts his own party or cause and joins the enemy.
